From what I gather, there are a couple of incidents where I confronted my mom about her parenting choices. The first time was about her not taking me to the doctor when I was younger, which almost cost me my life. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to recover on bed rest. I told her that's not okay and that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die. She didn't take it well but eventually brushed it off. Then, later, she asked me to get her a drink and said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded that I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, so I don't know anything about her. She got upset, cried, and accused me of trying to make her seem bad. I explained I wasn't trying to be mean, just pointing out that not taking kids to the doctor isn't cool, and that I don't know her because I didn't grow up with her. We went home, and a few weeks later, we went out again. Then, another incident happened with my brother's phone. I bought him a phone because they kept taking his, and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear that the other phone was strictly for him. But I found out they were taking and using that one too. When I confronted her, I told her I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished, but I will if she doesn't stop stealing it. I emphasized that it's his phone, I'm paying for it, and it's not hers to touch. I also mentioned that she keeps taking his work money, which is already bad enough. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly that she kind of is. She had a meltdown, sobbed, said she doesn't need me in her life, and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, the question is, AITA? (Am I the Asshole?) First, I need to consider the context. My mom has made some serious mistakes in parenting, especially regarding my health. She didn't take me to the doctor when I was younger, which led to a near-death experience. That's a significant issue. I confronted her about it, which is understandable because I was hurt and scared. However, the way I confronted her might have been harsh. She didn't take it well, but she eventually dropped it. Then, in the second incident, she made a comment about me knowing what she likes because she raised me. My response was to point out that my grandparents raised me, so I don't know her. That might have been a bit cold, especially since she was trying to get a drink. It's possible that my response made her feel unappreciated or misunderstood. In the third incident, regarding the phone, I was trying to protect my brother's belongings. I made it clear that the phone was for him, and I was upset when she took it. My approach was firm, but I didn't want my brother to be punished. However, when she accused me of treating her like a bad mother, I told her she kind of is. That was a direct and harsh statement, which likely hurt her feelings and led to her leaving. Now, considering all this, I need to evaluate whether my actions were justified or if I overstepped. On one hand, my mom's actions regarding my health were negligent and caused me serious harm. I have a right to express my feelings and concerns about that. However, the way I expressed it might have been too confrontational and hurtful. In the second incident, my response was cold and might have been unnecessary. It's possible that I could have handled the situation more gently, especially since she was asking for a drink and seemed to be trying to connect. In the third incident, while I was trying to protect my brother, my choice of words was harsh. Telling her she's a bad mother directly was likely too much, especially after she had a meltdown. It's possible that I could have addressed the issue without attacking her character. Overall, while my mom's actions were problematic, my approach in confronting her might have been too harsh and contributed to the conflict. It's important to communicate feelings and concerns, but doing so in a respectful and constructive manner can help prevent further issues. In this case, it seems like I might have been the asshole by being too confrontational and hurtful in my communication.
